Thought: This question is asking about a disadvantage of linear peptide scaffolds when used in chemical libraries for drug discovery. Let me think about the properties of linear peptides:

1. Linear peptides are flexible and can adopt many conformations
2. They are relatively easy to synthesize using standard peptide chemistry
3. There are plenty of reagents available for peptide synthesis
4. Linear peptides often have poor pharmacokinetic properties because:
   - They are susceptible to proteolytic degradation in the body
   - They typically have poor membrane permeability
   - They often have poor oral bioavailability
   - They may have short half-lives in circulation

Looking at the options:
A. Pharmacodynamic properties relate to how the drug affects the body (binding, efficacy)
B. Pharmacokinetic properties relate to how the body affects the drug (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion)
C. Linear peptides are actually relatively straightforward to synthesize
D. There are many reagents available for peptide synthesis

Based on my knowledge, linear peptides are known to have poor pharmacokinetic properties (option B), which is why cyclic peptides and other constrained scaffolds are often preferred in drug discovery.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
